Fast path takeover predicate and lock ownership encoding.
Wound-wait admission, kill, and victim selection rules.

findings.text: Lock event accounting is compile time optional. One build provides a counting operation parameterized by event name and one build defines the same operation as having no effect, so callers invoke it unconditionally.

Wound-wait support is a build time constant. One configuration reports absent and maps a base lock to no container, the other reports present and maps a base lock to its enclosing owner object. Blocking paths consult it before admission or kill handling.

Each blocking request associates one task with one base lock and carries two ordering nodes, a wake condition, and optional wound context. One node orders the request among contenders for the lock and the other orders it among inheritance donors for the owner. Keys combine normalized priority with deadline.

Waiter priority is normalized so ordinary priorities collapse to a single default level while real time and deadline priorities keep distinct values. The normalized value plus task deadline forms the comparison key for placement and for deciding whether propagation can stop.

Fresh waiters start with both ordering nodes empty, a normal wake condition, and no task. Filling the lock order key needs the waiter lock and an empty lock node. Mirroring it into the inheritance node additionally needs the task inheritance lock and an empty inheritance node. Debug builds poison storage on release.

Contention queues and per task donor sets are ordered trees with cached leftmost entries. Lock queue insertion and removal need the waiter lock. Donor insertion, removal, and reading the highest donor need the owner inheritance lock. Donor emptiness is directly testable and highest lock contender is observable under the waiter lock.

Enqueue on a contended base lock runs with the waiter lock held and briefly takes task inheritance locks to link the waiter and refresh donor state. A task already owning the target is rejected at once unless wound context is present, where cycle handling is deferred to logic tolerant of spurious cycles. Unowned locks finish after enqueue.

Blocking first links the waiter then optionally runs wound admission that can immediately withdraw the waiter and fail. If the new waiter becomes highest, the previous highest donor is replaced and owner priority is reevaluated. A chain walk is triggered only when the waiter is highest and the owner is itself blocked, or when detection mode requests it.

Priority propagation follows owners blocking on owners while holding at most one task reference across steps. After every lock drop it revalidates that the waiter still exists, the origin still has an owner, and the chain link is unchanged, aborting otherwise. Keys are refreshed on requeue because scheduler or deadline state may have changed underneath.

Whether the walk also searches for cycles depends on build and caller mode. Debug builds always detect, other builds detect only when the caller asks for full detection. Detection is disabled for wound participants so wound resolution wins, and a single wound class cycle is explicitly not reported as generic deadlock.

The walk is bounded by a configurable maximum depth. Exceeding it drops the held reference and reports deadlock, with a warning emitted only once per configured limit value identifying the initiating task. A cycle is otherwise reported when the walk revisits the origin lock or an owner equal to the initiator, unless wound origin converts it to success.

The walk takes a task inheritance lock before attempting its blocking lock, reversing normal order, so the second acquisition is a nonblocking attempt with retry and processor relaxation on failure. Lifetime safety comes from the inheritance lock pinning the blocking lock and from task references pinning tasks across drops.

Withdrawal dequeues the waiter and clears its blocked association even when never fully linked handling is needed. Only when the withdrawn waiter was highest and an owner exists does it refresh the owner donor set with the new highest contender and reevaluate owner priority. Further propagation uses minimal detection and is skipped when the owner is unblocked.

Slow acquisition loops over immediate takeover attempts while honoring timeout expiry, pending signals, and wound kill requests with distinct outcomes. Between attempts only a highest contender may briefly spin on a running owner, otherwise it sleeps in the requested state. Task state is restored to running on exit and accounting marks block, sleep, and acquisition.

Owner spinning is either wholly disabled or allowed only while owner identity is stable under read side protection, the owner stays scheduled, the spinner stays highest, and no reschedule is requested. Any violation stops spinning and falls back to sleeping.

Generic deadlock failure without an explicit detection request is fatal for non wound waiters: after releasing the waiter lock a warning is emitted and the caller sleeps indefinitely in interruptible state. Wound participants and callers that already requested detection simply propagate the error.

Owner priority reflects its highest inheritance donor. Replacing a donor needs both the waiter lock of the relevant base lock and the owner inheritance lock, with the caller guaranteeing that the named owner still owns that lock.
